# ProfileSample

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Language Features](Language-Features) · [Other](Language-Features-Other)

</div>


```blitzbasic
ProfileSample:Void file:String
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | In | String | required | The file that receives the samples, or an empty string to stop. |

## Description

Starts or stops recording where the program spends its time, like the environment variable `BLITZLLVM_PROFILE_SAMPLE` (which starts it with the program). The program is sampled every millisecond and the addresses go to the file. With `-g` or `-d` as well, `<file>.stacks` also receives the call stacks. See [[Environment-Variables]] for the files.

An empty name stops sampling and writes what is left.

Windows only, and only in a program that was compiled with `--profile`. Everywhere else this command does nothing.

## Differences

* This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the original has no such command.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
ProfileSample "sample.bin"
; ... the part of the program that is slow ...
ProfileSample ""
```
## Format of the call stack file

x64 Windows programs built with `--profile` and `-g` (or `-d`) write `<file>.stacks` next to `<file>`. The call stacks are not recorded without the symbols, as they could not be turned into names.

The file starts with a header, followed by one record per sample, in the order of `<file>`. It grows every four seconds. All numbers are little endian. The header holds the load address of the program, and each record holds one instruction address per sample.

| Header | Size | What |
|---|---|---|
| magic | 4 | `BBST` |
| version | 4 | `1` |
| max_frames | 4 | How many addresses a record has room for (`8`) |
| base | 8 | Where the program is loaded |

| Record | Size | What |
|---|---|---|
| frame | 4 | How many `Flip` calls there were before the sample, to cut the samples per phase |
| depth | 4 | How many of the addresses are used |
| microseconds | 8 | Since the sampler started |
| addresses | 8 * max_frames | Where the sample was, then the return addresses of the callers (subtract `base` and look up in the debug information) |
